record.title: Dyson's crank limiting-shape conjecture
record.statement:
Let $M(m,n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$ with crank $m$, where the crank of a partition is the largest part if it has no ones, and otherwise is the number of parts strictly larger than its number of ones minus its number of ones. Let $p(n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$, and set

$$
\beta:=\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{6n}}.
$$

**Dyson's crank limiting-shape conjecture.** As $n\to\infty$,

$$
M(m,n)\sim \frac14\beta\,\operatorname{sech}^2\left(\frac12\beta m\right)p(n).
$$

The conjecture describes the limiting shape of the crank generating function and was solved in the paper, although the supplied parser metadata does not give a resolution status beyond the paper's assertion that it solves Dyson's conjecture.
record.source_name: Kathrin Bringmann and Jehanne Dousse, “On Dyson's crank conjecture and the uniform asymptotic behavior of certain inverse theta functions”, arXiv:1311.6089 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.6089

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2013). “This conjecture was proven by Atkin and Swinnerton-Dyer .”

record.title: Heuristic least-nonresidue bound from a quadratic twist
record.statement:
Let $\xi$ be an odd primitive Dirichlet character modulo $k$ with $3\nmid k$, and define

$$
\chi(n):=\xi(n)\left(\frac{n}{3}\right).
$$
 Let $n_\xi$ denote the least positive integer $n$ with $\xi(n)\neq 1$, and let $M(\chi)$ denote the maximum size of the partial sums of $\chi$. **Heuristic conjecture.** One expects that

$$
\log n_\xi\leq\left(\frac{\pi}{e^\gamma}+o(1)\right)\frac{M(\chi)}{\sqrt{k}}.
$$
 This is presented as a heuristic consequence suggesting that the preceding bounds are not optimal; it would relate the least nonresidue directly to one specific quadratic twist and could sharpen estimates for least nonresidues if proved.
record.source_name: Jonathan Bober and Leo Goldmakher, “Pólya-Vinogradov and the least quadratic nonresidue”, arXiv:1311.7556 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.7556

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2013).

record.title: Kohn's unknotting-crossing conjecture for minimal diagrams
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a knot, and let $u(K)$ denote its unknotting number. An **unknotting crossing** is a crossing whose change produces the unknot, and a **minimal diagram** is a diagram of $K$ with the minimum possible number of crossings.

**Kohn's conjecture.** If

$$
u(K)=1,
$$

then $K$ has an unknotting crossing in a minimal diagram.

This conjecture has been resolved in a number of cases, as stated in the source; the supplied status evidence therefore records it as solved.
record.source_name: Duncan McCoy, “Alternating knots with unknotting number one”, arXiv:1312.1278 (2014).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2006–2013). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:0902.1573](https://arxiv.org/abs/0902.1573), [arXiv:math/0601265](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0601265).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.1278

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of December 2013). “This has been resolved in a number of cases.”

record.title: Eigenvalue criterion for many edge-disjoint spanning trees
record.statement:
Let $d\geq 8$ and $4\leq k\leq \left\lfloor\frac{d}{2}\right\rfloor$ be two integers. Let $G$ be a $d$-regular graph, and write $\lambda_2(G)$ for its second largest eigenvalue. **The eigenvalue criterion conjecture.** If

$$
\lambda_2(G)<d-\frac{2k-1}{d+1},
$$

then $G$ contains at least $k$ edge-disjoint spanning trees. This conjecture extends the paper's established sufficient condition for $k\in\{2,3\}$ to the range $d\geq 8$ and $4\leq k\leq\left\lfloor d/2\right\rfloor$; the supplied text gives no resolution of these additional cases.
record.source_name: Sebastian M. Cioabă and Wiseley Wong, “Edge-disjoint spanning trees and eigenvalues of regular graphs”, arXiv:1312.2245 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.2245

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2013).

record.title: The convex-tile inverse Grünbaum–Shephard conjecture for spherical monohedral tilings
record.statement:
A **spherical monohedral tiling** is a tiling of the sphere by congruent tiles, and it is **normal** when its tiles meet edge-to-edge in the usual locally finite way. A tiling is **isohedral** when its symmetry group acts transitively on its tiles. An **Archimedean dual** is the dual of an Archimedean spherical tiling; an $n$-gonal bipyramid and an $n$-gonal trapezohedron are the corresponding stated spherical topological types.

**Convex-tile inverse Grünbaum–Shephard conjecture.** For every normal spherical monohedral tiling topologically a Platonic solid, an Archimedean dual, an $n$-gonal bipyramid, or an $n$-gonal trapezohedron, with $n\ge3$, if the tile is convex, then the tiling is isohedral.

The conjecture proposes an inverse to a result of Grünbaum and Shephard under convexity. The paper establishes the assertion for convex quadrangles over pseudo-double wheels, while concave examples show that convexity is essential; the general claim remains open in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Yohji Akama and Yudai Sakano, “Spherical tilings by congruent quadrangles over pseudo-double wheels (III) - the essential uniqueness in case of convex tiles”, arXiv:1312.3026 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.3026

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2013).

record.title: Ryan–Pomerance conjecture on divisibility of maximal divisor heights
record.statement:
Let $p$ be a fixed odd prime and let $b$ be a fixed positive integer. For a positive integer $n$, define

$$
B(n):=\max\{H(f): f\mid x^n-1,\ f\in\mathbb{Z}[x]\},
$$

where $H(f)$ is the largest absolute value of a coefficient of $f$. **Ryan–Pomerance divisibility conjecture.** As $q$ ranges over primes with $p<q$, every value in the finite list $B(pq^b)$ is divisible by $p$. This conjecture concerns the arithmetic structure of maximal heights of integral polynomial divisors of $x^{pq^b}-1$; the source presents it as a conjecture of Ryan and collaborators, without giving a resolution.
record.source_name: Shaozu Wang, “Maximal height of divisors of x^pq^b-1”, arXiv:1312.3108 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.3108

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2013).

record.title: The local-global conjecture for Apollonian 3-circle packings
record.statement:
Fix a primitive Apollonian 3-circle packing $\mathcal{P}$, let $\mathcal{K}$ be its set of curvatures, and let $A_{\mathcal{P}}$ be the set of admissible integers, meaning integers that pass all local obstructions for $\mathcal{P}$.

**Local-global conjecture.** Every sufficiently large admissible integer from $\mathcal{P}$ is a curvature. Equivalently,

$$
\#\{n\in\mathcal{K}\mid n\leq N\}=\#\{n\in A_{\mathcal{P}}\mid 0<n\leq N\}+O(1).
$$

The conjecture asserts that the local congruence conditions determine all sufficiently large curvatures in an Apollonian 3-packing. The paper proves a density-one version of this statement; the full conjecture is left open in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Xin Zhang, “On the Local-Global Principle for Integral Apollonian-3 Circle Packings”, arXiv:1312.4650 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.4650

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of December 2013).

record.title: Li et al.'s rational sign-pattern minimum-rank conjecture
record.statement:
Let $S$ be a sign pattern matrix, let $t$ be its term rank, and let $r$ be the minimum rank of $S$ over the reals. The term rank is the smallest number of rows and columns needed to include all nonzero entries of the matrix.

**Li et al.'s conjecture.** If $r\geqslant t-2$, then the minimum rank of $S$ over the rationals is also $r$.

The conjecture concerns when the minimum rank of a sign pattern over the rationals agrees with its minimum rank over the reals. The paper states that it proves this conjecture and gives examples showing the optimality of the result.
record.source_name: Yaroslav Shitov, “Sign patterns of rational matrices with large rank”, arXiv:1312.5369 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.5369

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of December 2013); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Rational minimum-rank conjecture for sign patterns with at most three zeros per column
record.statement:
Let ${\cal A}$ be a sign pattern, and let $mr({\cal A})$ denote its minimum rank over the reals while $mr_{\mathbb Q}({\cal A})$ denotes its minimum rank over the rationals. **Rational minimum-rank conjecture.** If

$$
m r({\cal A})=3,
$$

and each column of ${\cal A}$ contains at most three zero entries, then

$$
mr_{\mathbb Q}({\cal A})=mr({\cal A}).
$$

The preceding theorem establishes the analogous conclusion when each column contains at most two zeros; the conjecture addresses the remaining three-zero case, motivated by the absence of known non-rationally realizable point-line configurations with at most three points on each line.
record.source_name: Guangming Jing, Wei Gao, Yubin Gao, Fei Gong, Zhongshan Li, Yanling Shao and Lihua Zhang, “Sign patterns with minimum rank 3 and point-line configurations”, arXiv:1312.6162 (2013).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1312.6048](https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.6048).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.6162

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2013).

record.title: The entropy lower-bound conjecture for graphs with a given degree sequence
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a strict graphic sequence of type $\varepsilon$, and let $H_{1}(x)$ be the entropy function whose maximum is attained at $\widetilde{\mathbf{p}}$. Write $\mathbb{G}^{D}$ for the set of graphs with degree sequence $D$. **Entropy lower-bound conjecture.** There exists a number $\eta>0$ independent of $n$ such that

$$
e^{-\eta n\cdot\log(n)}\cdot e^{H_{1}(\widetilde{\mathbf{p}})}\leq\left|\mathbb{G}^{D}\right|\leq e^{H_{1}(\widetilde{\mathbf{p}})}.
$$

The upper bound is the easy part and follows from the entropy estimate, while the lower bound is explicitly identified as open. This conjecture would provide the needed estimate for the number of graphs with the prescribed degree sequence.
record.source_name: Behzad Mehrdad, “Trees in Random Sparse Graphs with a Given Degree Sequence”, arXiv:1401.0220 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0220

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2014). “However, the lower bound that is crucial for our next Conjecture is open.”

record.title: Undecidability of profinite triviality for hyperbolic groups
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a hyperbolic group, and let $\widehat{\Gamma}$ denote its profinite completion.

**Hyperbolic profinite-triviality conjecture.** There is no algorithm that can determine whether or not a given hyperbolic group $\Gamma$ has

$$
\widehat{\Gamma}\cong 1.
$$

The conjecture proposes undecidability of the triviality problem for profinite completions in the hyperbolic case. The source notes that the triviality problem is solvable for hyperbolic groups, and explains that the conjecture would be false if every non-trivial hyperbolic group had non-trivial profinite completion; its status is therefore not settled by the supplied text.
record.source_name: Martin R. Bridson and Henry Wilton, “The triviality problem for profinite completions”, arXiv:1401.2273 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.2273

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of January 2014). “Since the triviality problem is solvable for hyperbolic groups, the above conjecture is false if every non-trivial hyperbolic group $\Gamma$ has $\widehat{\Gamma}\ncong 1$.”

record.title: Sublinear polynomial upper bound for the on-line ranking number of trees
record.statement:
Let $T$ be an $n$-vertex tree with maximum degree $k$, and let $\mathring{\rho}(T)$ denote its on-line ranking number.

**On-line ranking conjecture.** There exist universal constants $a$ and $b$ satisfying $0<a<1<b$ such that

$$
\mathring{\rho}(T)\leq b(kn)^a.
$$

This conjecture proposes a general upper bound for the on-line ranking number of trees, analogous to the bounds established for the trees $T_{k,d}$ in the paper. The supplied context does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Daniel C. McDonald, “On-line vertex ranking of trees”, arXiv:1401.2669 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.2669

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2014).

record.title: The path–linear-forest quasar Ramsey number conjecture
record.statement:
Let $P_n$ be the path on $n$ vertices, let $F$ be a non-empty linear forest on $m$ vertices, let $K_1\vee F$ denote the join of $F$ with a single vertex, and let $o(F)$ be the number of odd-order components of $F$. **Path–linear-forest quasar Ramsey conjecture.** If

$$
n\geq 2\quad\text{and}\quad n+1\leq m\leq 2n-1,
$$

then

$$
R(P_n,K_1\vee F)=\max\left\{2n-1,\left\lceil\frac{3m}{2}\right\rceil-1, m+n-o(F)-2\right\}.
$$

This would determine the remaining Ramsey numbers of paths versus proper quasars of the form $K_1\vee F$ in the range $n+1\leq m\leq 2n-1$; the preceding results establish matching bounds when every component of $F$ has even order, but the general case is left open.
record.source_name: Binlong Li and Bo Ning, “On path-quasar Ramsey numbers”, arXiv:1401.3545 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.3545

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2014).

record.title: Logarithmic injectivity-radius conjecture for random mapping tori
record.statement: Let $S$ be a surface, and let $N$ denote the length of a random monodromy word defining a mapping torus of $S$. The **injectivity radius** is the radius of the largest embedded metric ball at a point, minimized over the manifold. **Logarithmic injectivity-radius conjecture.** The injectivity radius of a random mapping torus of $S$ decays as $1/\log^2 N$. The estimate follows for the generating set of $\operatorname{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ discussed in the paper from maximal runs in random words; its validity for general generating sets is left as a conjecture.
record.source_name: Igor Rivin, “Statistics of Random 3-Manifolds occasionally fibering over the circle”, arXiv:1401.5736 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.5736

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2014).

record.title: Liu–Sousa conjecture on monochromatic triangle decompositions
record.statement:
Let $k\geq 2$, and let $\phi_k(n,K_3)$ denote the maximum, over $k$-edge-coloured graphs on $n$ vertices, of the minimum number of parts in a monochromatic $K_3$-decomposition. Let $R_k(3)$ be the $k$-colour Ramsey number of the triangle, and let $t_{R_k(3)-1}(n)$ be the number of edges in the Turán graph $T_{R_k(3)-1}(n)$. **Liu–Sousa conjecture.** If $k\geq 4$, then

$$
\phi_k(n,K_3)=t_{R_k(3)-1}(n)
$$

for $n\geq R_k(3)$. The cited results establish the corresponding equality for $k=2,3$ and sufficiently large $n$, but the stated case $k\geq 4$ is presented without a resolution and remains open.
record.source_name: Henry Liu, Oleg Pikhurko and Teresa Sousa, “Monochromatic Clique Decompositions of Graphs”, arXiv:1401.6345 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.6345

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2014). “For every graph $G$, we have $\tau_3(G) \leq 2\nu_3(G).$ Conjecture remains open although many partial results have been proved.”

record.title: Characterization of class III graphs for the adjacent vertex distinguishing index by sum
record.statement:
For a graph $\Gamma$, let $tndi_{\sum}(\Gamma)$ be the minimum number of colors in a proper total coloring distinguishing adjacent vertices by sums. The graph is called $tndi_{\sum}$ class III when $tndi_{\sum}(\Gamma)=\Delta(\Gamma)+3$, where $\Delta(\Gamma)$ is its maximum degree. **Class III characterization conjecture.** A graph $\Gamma$ is $tndi_{\sum}$ class III if and only if

$$
\Gamma=K_{2n+1}
$$

for some $n\geq 1$. This proposes that the odd complete graphs are exactly the extremal graphs for the adjacent vertex distinguishing index by sum.
record.source_name: Hana Choi, Dongseok Kim, Sungjin Lee and Yeonhee Lee, “A proper total coloring distinguishing adjacent vertices by sums of some product graphs”, arXiv:1402.0615 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.0615

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2014).

record.title: NP-completeness of PL realizability for 2-hypergraphs in three dimensions
record.statement: A 2-hypergraph is a hypergraph whose hyperedges have size two, and **PL realizability** in $\mathbb R^d$ means realizability by a piecewise-linear representation in $\mathbb R^d$. **The PL realizability conjecture.** (a) Deciding whether a 2-hypergraph is PL realizable in $\mathbb R^3$ is NP-complete. (b) Deciding whether a 2-hypergraph is PL realizable in $\mathbb R^4$ is decidable. The supplied text is corrupted and does not identify this passage as a conjecture or provide enough reliable context to determine its intended status.
record.source_name: Arkadiy Skopenkov, “Realizability of hypergraphs and intrinsic link theory”, arXiv:1402.0658 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.0658

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2014). “This conjecture was proved only in 1978 by Brian Ummel , cf. Theorem below.”

record.title: Edge-colouring conjecture for d-interval hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a hypergraph of $d$-intervals. Let $\chi_e(H)$ denote its edge chromatic number, and let $\Delta$ be the maximum degree of a point on any line. **Edge-colouring conjecture.** Then

$$
\chi_e(H) \le d\Delta.
$$
 For $d=2$, this strengthens the previously raised conjecture that the edge chromatic number is at most twice the maximum size of an intersecting subhypergraph. The bound is presented as a conjectural consequence suggested by the weighted fractional-covering framework and remains open.
record.source_name: Ron Aharoni, Tomas Kaiser and Shira Zerbib, “Fractional covers and matchings in families of weighted d-intervals”, arXiv:1402.2064 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.2064

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2014). “An open question in is whether $\tau^*<3$ for intersecting families of (non-separated) 2-intervals.”

record.title: Conjecture on the asymptotic second eigenvalue of the Schoenberg operator
record.statement:
Let $\gamma_{\Delta_n,k}$ denote the second largest eigenvalue of the Schoenberg operator associated with the fixed grid $\Delta_n$ and spline degree $k$.

**Schoenberg eigenvalue conjecture.** For fixed $k>0$,

$$
\gamma_{\Delta_n,k}\to 1\quad\text{as }n\to\infty.
$$

For fixed $n>0$,

$$
\gamma_{\Delta_n,k}\to 1\quad\text{as }k\to\infty.
$$

The conjecture concerns whether the second largest eigenvalue can affect the convergence rate in the lower approximation bound. The source states that the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of the Schoenberg operator are otherwise unknown and provides no resolution.
record.source_name: Johannes Nagler, Paula Cerejeiras and Brigitte Forster, “Lower bounds for the approximation with variation-diminishing splines”, arXiv:1402.2403 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.2403

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2014).

record.title: The product-order minimum conjecture for bidegrees of curves
record.statement:
Let $C/k$ be a curve, and let

$$
S_{1,1}(C)=\left\{(a,b)\in\mathbb{N}^2\mid a\leq b\text{ and }C\simeq\text{ a curve of bidegree }(a,b)\text{ in }\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1\right\},
$$

where $\simeq$ denotes birational equivalence. **Product-order minimum conjecture.** The set $S_{1,1}(C)$ admits a minimum with respect to the product order $\leq\times\leq$ on $\mathbb{N}^2$. The conjecture concerns whether the bidegree invariant is independent of choosing a monomial order; no resolution is given here.
record.source_name: Wouter Castryck and Filip Cools, “The lattice size of a lattice polygon”, arXiv:1402.4652 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.4652

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2014).

record.title: The centralizer fusion-system conjecture for normal pairs
record.statement:
Let $((S,\mathcal{F}),(T,\mathcal{E}))$ be a normal pair of fusion systems realized by a normal pair $(G,H)$ of finite groups. Write $O_{p'}(H)$ for the largest normal subgroup of $H$ of order prime to $p$. Let $C_S(H)$ be the centralizer of $H$ in $S$, $C_G(H)$ the centralizer of $H$ in $G$, and $\mathcal{F}_{C_S(H)}(C_G(H))$ the fusion system induced by $C_G(H)$ on $C_S(H)$. **Centralizer fusion-system conjecture.** If $O_{p'}(H)=1$, then

$$
C_\mathcal{F}(\mathcal{E})=\mathcal{F}_{C_S(H)}(C_G(H)).
$$

This strengthens the preceding proposed equality by identifying the entire centralizer fusion system, rather than only its underlying centralizer subgroup. The source gives no resolution evidence, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Jason Semeraro, “Centralizers of Subsystems of Fusion Systems”, arXiv:1402.4981 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.4981

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of February 2014). “So far, all attempts to construct a counterexample to this conjecture have failed.”

record.title: The Chen–Fu–Kim–Stehr–Watts extremal spectral-radius conjecture for bipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple bipartite graph with bipartition orders $p$ and $q$, and let $\mathcal{K}(p,q,e)$ denote the family of $e$-edge subgraphs of the complete bipartite graph $K_{p,q}$. Write $\rho(G)$ for the largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix of $G$. For integers $1<e<pq$, **the bipartite extremal spectral-radius conjecture.** An extremal graph attaining

$$
\max_{G\in\mathcal{K}(p,q,e)}\rho(G)
$$

is obtained from a complete bipartite graph by adding one vertex and a corresponding number of edges. This conjecture asks for the maximum spectral radius among bipartite graphs with fixed bipartition orders and edge count; the source notes that the case $e=pq-2$ was proved, while the general assertion is refined by subsequent conjectures.
record.source_name: Chia-an Liu and Chih-wen Weng, “Spectral Radius of Bipartite Graphs”, arXiv:1402.5621 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.5621

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2014).

record.title: The general refined extremal spectral-radius conjecture for bipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple bipartite graph in $\mathcal{K}(p,q,e)$, the family of $e$-edge subgraphs of $K_{p,q}$. For positive integers $s\leq p$ and $t\leq q$, let $K_{s,t}^{\{e\}}$ denote the graph obtained from $K_{s,t}$ by deleting $st-e$ edges incident on a common vertex in the partite set of order no less than that of the other partite set. Write $\rho(G)$ for the largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix. **The general refined extremal spectral-radius conjecture.** For some positive integers $s\leq p$ and $t\leq q$ satisfying

$$
0\leq st-e\leq\min(s,t),
$$

one has

$$
\rho(G)\leq\rho(K_{s,t}^{\{e\}}).
$$

This is proposed as a general refinement of the first extremal conjecture. The source proves the dense special case above but does not state a resolution of this general refinement.
record.source_name: Chia-an Liu and Chih-wen Weng, “Spectral Radius of Bipartite Graphs”, arXiv:1402.5621 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.5621

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2014).

record.title: The corrected bipartite decomposition conjecture for random graphs
record.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph, and let $\tau(G)$ denote the minimum number of pairwise edge-disjoint complete bipartite subgraphs of $G$ whose edges partition $E$. Let $\beta(G)$ denote the graph parameter used in the paper's corrected formulation. For the random graph $G=G(n,0.5)$, **the corrected bipartite decomposition conjecture.**

$$
\tau(G)=n-\beta(G)+1
$$

with high probability. This is presented as a plausible slight variation of the refuted Erdős conjecture; the supplied text gives no resolution, so its status remains open.
record.source_name: Noga Alon, “Bipartite decomposition of random graphs”, arXiv:1402.6466 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.6466

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2014).

record.title: The quarter-bias conjecture for bit-commitment coin-flipping protocols
record.statement:
Let a **strong coin-flipping protocol based on bit-commitment** be any protocol in the family formally defined in Section~, and let its bias be the maximum excess of either party's cheating probability over $1/2$. **Quarter-bias conjecture.** Every such protocol has bias at least

$$
\frac{1}{4}.
$$

The conjecture is based on computational searches over the parameterized protocol family, including zoning-in tests around protocols with bias $1/4$; resolving whether all protocols in the family satisfy this bound remains an open problem.
record.source_name: Ashwin Nayak, Jamie Sikora and Levent Tunçel, “A search for quantum coin-flipping protocols using optimization techniques”, arXiv:1403.0505 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.0505

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2014). “An obvious open problem is to resolve the conjecture that all the protocols in the family we study have bias at least $1/4$.”

record.title: Fischer–Riegler multivariate Laurent polynomial inversion conjecture
record.statement:
For integers $s,t\geq 0$, define the rational function

$$
P_{s,t}(z_1,\ldots,z_{s+t-1}):=\prod_{i=1}^{s}z_i^{2s-2i-t+1}(1-z_i^{-1})^{i-1}\prod_{i=s+1}^{s+t-1}z_i^{2i-2s-t}(1-z_i^{-1})^s\prod_{1\leq p<q\leq s+t-1}\frac{1-z_p+z_pz_q}{z_q-z_p}.
$$

Let $\operatorname{\mathbf{Sym}}$ be the unnormalized symmetrizer, $\operatorname{\mathbf{Sym}}p(z_1,\ldots,z_n)=\sum_{\sigma\in\mathcal S_n}p(z_{\sigma(1)},\ldots,z_{\sigma(n)})$, and set $R_{s,t}=\operatorname{\mathbf{Sym}}P_{s,t}$. 

**Fischer–Riegler Laurent polynomial inversion conjecture.** If $s\leq t$, then for every $i\in\{1,\ldots,s+t-1\}$,

$$
R_{s,t}(z_1,\ldots,z_{s+t-1})=R_{s,t}(z_1,\ldots,z_{i-1},z_i^{-1},z_{i+1},\ldots,z_{s+t-1}).
$$

The identity is the paper's main more general conjecture and would imply the refined VSASM formula through the associated linear equation system. Only partial results are presented in the source.
record.source_name: Ilse Fischer and Lukas Riegler, “Vertically symmetric alternating sign matrices and a multivariate Laurent polynomial identity”, arXiv:1403.0535 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.0535

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2014).

record.title: The critical-number conjecture for dense triangle-free binary matroids
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a simple triangle-free binary matroid, let $r(M)$ denote its rank, and let $|M|$ denote its number of elements. The **critical number** of $M$ is the minimum codimension of a flat of the ambient projective geometry disjoint from $E(M)$. **Dense triangle-free binary matroid conjecture.** For each real number $\alpha>0$ there exists $c\in\mathbb Z$ such that, if

$$
|M|\geq \alpha 2^{r(M)},
$$

then $M$ has critical number at most $c$. The conjecture would extend the paper's main theorem from odd circuit lengths $k\geq 5$ to triangles; the graph analogue fails for triangle-free graphs, so the binary-matroid assertion is a distinct structural question.

record.title: The compatible-pair module-structure conjecture for second cohomology
record.statement: Let $R$ be a pro-p-group with a uniserial $R$-module $T$ and lower $R$-central series $T=T_0geq T_1geq T_2geqcdots$. For each $n$, write $\operatorname{Comp}(R,T/T_n)$ for the group of compatible pairs acting on $H^2(R,T/T_n)$, and similarly write $\operatorname{Comp}(R,T)$ for the compatible pairs acting on $H^2(R,T)$. **The compatible-pair module-structure conjecture.** For every $n\gg0$, the $\operatorname{Comp}(R,T/T_n)$-module structure of $H^2(R,T/T_n)$ coincides with its $\operatorname{Comp}(R,T)$-module structure: for every compatible pair $(\beta,\epsilon)\in\operatorname{Comp}(R,T/T_n)$, there exists a compatible pair $(\beta,\delta)\in\operatorname{Comp}(R,T)$ inducing the same automorphism of $H^2(R,T/T_n)$. The claim was used to identify the relevant compatible-pair actions in the classification of prime-power groups by coclass, but it is false: the corrigendum gives a counterexample in its counterexample section.
record.source_name: Martin Couson, “Corrigendum to "On the classification of prime-power groups by coclass"”, arXiv:1403.2091 (2014).

record.title: Golden-ratio conjecture for normalized dilatations
record.statement: Let $S$ be a closed surface and let $\phi$ be a pseudo-Anosov mapping class with dilatation $\lambda(\phi)$. For a fibered cohomology class, let $L(S,\phi)$ denote the corresponding normalized dilatation; in the genus-$g$ family considered in the paper, $L(S_{(1,g)},\phi_{(1,g)})=\lambda(\phi_{(1,g)})^{2g}$. The **golden-ratio normalized-dilatation conjecture.** The smallest accumulation point for normalized dilatations is $\gamma_0^4$, where $\gamma_0$ is the golden ratio. This is presented as a more general version of the genus-normalized conjecture and is motivated by a family whose normalized dilatations converge to $\gamma_0^4$; its resolution is not supplied here.

record.title: Pseudo-dimension matching limit for dense graph sequences
record.statement:
Let $G_n$ be a sequence of graphs admitting a graphon limit $\mathcal{G}$, with edge weights following a distribution of pseudo-dimension $q$. Suppose that there exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that the measure on $[0,1]^2$ given by $\mathcal{G}$ has density at least $\varepsilon$ everywhere, and let $M(G_n)$ denote the minimum total weight of a perfect matching. **Dense graph matching conjecture.** The quantity

$$
n^{-1+1/q}M(G_n)
$$

converges in probability to a constant depending only on $q$ and $\mathcal{G}$. This is presented as a speculation extending the proved convergence result for complete bipartite graphs; the source does not provide a resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Joel Larsson, “The Minimum Perfect Matching in Pseudo-dimension 0<q<1”, arXiv:1403.3635 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.3635

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2014). “This was later established independently by Nair, Prabhakar and Shaw and Wästlund , both using inductive proofs.”

record.title: The generator-commutator conjecture for regular finite W-superalgebras
record.statement: Let $\frak g$ be a basic classical Lie superalgebra, let $\chi$ be regular, and let $W_\chi$ be the associated finite W-superalgebra. Let $\pi$ denote the relevant quotient or representation map and let $Z(\frak g)$ be the center of $\frak g$. **Generator-commutator conjecture.** It is possible to find a set of generators of $W_\chi$ such that the even generators commute, and the commutators of odd generators belong to $\pi(Z(\frak g))$. This asserts a particularly controlled generating system for regular finite W-superalgebras; the supplied text gives no resolution or partial-result evidence.

record.title: Generalized Yau conjecture for semi-negative holomorphic sectional curvature
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a projective manifold with a Kähler metric of semi-negative holomorphic sectional curvature. Define $r_M$ as the invariant measuring the largest codimension of a maximal subspace in a tangent space on which the holomorphic sectional curvature vanishes. The **generalized Yau conjecture.** The Kodaira dimension satisfies

$$
\operatorname{kod}(M)\geq r_M.
$$

In particular, if $r_M=\dim M$, then the canonical line bundle $K_M$ is ample. This generalizes the negative-curvature case and would relate the curvature condition to positivity of the canonical bundle; the source presents it as a conjectural strengthening, while proving partial results and the stated special-case consequences.

record.title: Hajek's multinomial maximum conjecture
record.statement:
Let $k,n$ be positive integers. For each $j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}$, let $S_j$ be the collection of subsets $L\subseteq[n]^k$ such that $|L|=n$ and no two distinct elements of $L$ have the same $j$th coordinate. Set

$$
S=\bigcup_{j=1}^k S_j
$$

and define

$$
F_{n,k}(x)=\sum_{L\in S}\prod_{i\in L}x_i.
$$

Let $\Delta_{n^k}$ denote the standard simplex. **Hajek's conjecture.** On $\Delta_{n^k}$, the function $F_{n,k}$ attains its maximum only at

$$
\left(\frac{1}{n^k},\ldots,\frac{1}{n^k}\right).
$$

The conjecture arose from work on hashing and asserts uniqueness of the uniform maximizer. The supplied text gives no resolution evidence.
record.source_name: Codrut Grosu, “On the algebraic and topological structure of the set of Turán densities”, arXiv:1403.4653 (2016).
record.references:

record.title: Conjecture on minimal degree relations and Arnold exponents of hypersurfaces
record.statement:
Let $V:f=0$ be a projective hypersurface of degree $d$ in $\mathbb{P}^n$ with only weighted homogeneous isolated singularities. Let $mdr(V)$ denote the minimal degree of a nontrivial relation among the partial derivatives of $f$, and let $\alpha_V$ be the minimum of the Arnold exponents of the singularities of $V$. **The minimal-degree-relation conjecture.**

$$
mdr(V)\geq d\alpha_V-n.
$$

The formula is motivated by the corresponding computation for the complete-intersection family and is known in the case $n=2$ by the cited result; the supplied text gives no resolution in general.
record.source_name: Alexandru Dimca and Dorin Popescu, “Hilbert series and Lefschetz properties of dimension one almost complete intersections”, arXiv:1403.5921 (2014).

record.title: Landweber–Stong depth conjecture for finite general linear groups
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a subgroup of $GL_n({\mathbb F}_q)$ acting on $S={\mathbb F}_q[\mathbf{x}]$, and let $D_{n,j}$ denote the Dickson polynomials. **Landweber–Stong conjecture.** The depth of the invariant ring $S^H$ is the maximum integer $i$ for which

$$
D_{n,n-i},D_{n,n-i+1},\ldots,D_{n,n-2},D_{n,n-1}
$$

form a regular sequence on $S^H$. The source notes that this conjecture was proven when $q=p$ is prime by Bourguiba and Zarati; the general case is not resolved in the supplied text.

record.title: The conjectured exact value of the Möbius triangular-ratio Lipschitz constant
record.statement:
For $a\in (0,1)$, let $C(a)$ be the class of all Möbius transformations $h:\mathbb{B}^n\rightarrow\mathbb{B}^n$ satisfying $|h(0)|=a$, and define

$$
L(a)=\sup\left\{\frac{s_{\mathbb{B}^n}(h(x),h(y))}{s_{\mathbb{B}^n}(x,y)}:x,y\in\mathbb{B}^n,\ x\neq y,\ h\in C(a)\right\}.
$$

**The conjectured value of $L(a)$.** For $n=2$, numerical experiments suggest that

$$
L(a)=1+a.
$$

The preceding theorem proves the lower bound $L(a)\geq 1+a$ in dimension two, so the conjecture concerns the matching upper bound and would determine the optimal constant in the corresponding triangular-ratio metric estimate for conformal self-maps of the disk.
record.source_name: Jiaolong Chen, Parisa Hariri, Riku Klén and Matti Vuorinen, “Lipschitz conditions, triangular ratio metric, and quasiconformal maps”, arXiv:1403.6582 (2015).

record.title: Conjecture on the potential energy of a biased random walk on a tree
record.statement: Let $(X_n)_{n\geq 0}$ be the random walk in a random environment on a tree, let $V(X_n)$ denote its potential energy, and let $\mathbb{P}$ be the governing probability measure. Assume $$ and $$. **Potential-energy conjecture.** Under $\mathbb{P}$, on the set of non-extinction, $\frac{V(X_n)}{\log n}$ converges weakly to a limit law which is finite and strictly positive. This conjecture predicts that the potential energy at time $n$ has logarithmic scale, much smaller than the maximum potential energy up to time $n$, whose almost-sure growth is $\frac12(\log n)^2$ under the stated assumptions. The source presents this as an expectation, and gives no resolution.

record.title: Optimality of the square lattice among Steiner networks
record.statement: Let the cities be the points $\{(i,j): i,j\in\mathbb{Z}\}$ in the plane, and consider a Steiner network on this square-grid configuration. Its **normalized length** is its total network length per unit area, and its **stretch** is the maximum ratio between network distance and Euclidean distance for pairs of cities. **Square-grid Steiner-network optimality conjecture.** If a Steiner network on the square-grid configuration has stretch at most $\sqrt{2}$, then its normalized length is at least $2$. The usual square-lattice network has normalized length $2$ and stretch $\sqrt{2}$, so the conjecture asserts its optimality among Steiner networks with stretch at most $\sqrt{2}$.
